content: {"id":"01a0fa0b-9d8c-76a1-bf70-2d4e901bfe4c","created":true,"summary":"Releases ship automatically on every merge to main; no release tags"}

With the new setup, you don't cut a release. Merging to `main` is the release: once your change is merged, it ships automatically. You no longer push a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag. The old rule against publishing by hand probably still applies, since the pipeline does the publishing.

I couldn't confirm this in the code. The CI config isn't in this repo, so there was nothing here to check against.

I also updated the project memory. The old note said "release by pushing a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag," and I've marked it as challenged, quoting what you told me. I replaced it with a new note saying every merge to `main` ships automatically and there are no release tags. That way other sessions and collaborators won't be told to tag releases anymore.
